name: ci

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

jobs:
  smoke:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
      - name: Syntax-check every .cjs / .js
        run: |
          shopt -s globstar nullglob
          for f in **/*.cjs **/*.js; do
            case "$f" in node_modules/*) continue;; esac
            node --check "$f"
          done
      - name: Install (no secrets required)
        run: npm install --no-audit --no-fund || true
      - name: Test (runs against the zero-dependency echo path)
        run: npm test

--- ## Why Sentience Loop An agent that says "I'm improving" is emitting a sentence. An agent that predicted "error rate stays above 3/hr for two hours," logged it with 0.6 confidence and a timestamp, and later scored itself wrong is producing a measurement. Sentience Loop is the machinery for the second kind. It is a closed predictive-processing loop — perceive, predict, score, surprise, reflect, record — that turns claims into falsifiable, timestamped bets and grades them when they come due. Surprises (confident predictions that missed) are the highest-signal events: each one writes a belief-update so the next prediction is better calibrated. Every stage is fail-open (a broken sensor logs and is skipped, never crashes the tick) and every cycle appends an auditable record. Point the sensors at anything that emits signal — logs, metrics, a queue, an API — supply a scorer that reads ground truth, and let the loop keep an honest account of how well it actually understands its world. --- ## What it does | Module | What it does | Signal | |---|---|---| | **sensor bus** | Runs the sensors you register; each returns typed signals, a thrower is logged and skipped | perceive from anything | | **prediction ledger** | Falsifiable predictions with confidence + a test-after horizon, deduped within a window | claims become bets | | **scorer + surprise** | Grades matured predictions against ground truth; a confident miss writes a belief-update | learn from being wrong | --- ## Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR S["sensors\n(you plug in)"] --> P["PERCEIVE\nsignals"] P --> PR["PREDICT\nfalsifiable + confidence"] PR --> SC["SCORE\nmatured predictions"] SC --> SU["SURPRISE\nconfident miss"] SU --> BU[("belief-updates")] SU --> RF["REFLECT"] RF --> RE["RECORD\ncycle ledger"] BU -.-> PR SC -.-> RE classDef acc fill:#2a3157,stroke:#8B9EF5,color:#fff; class PR acc; class SC acc; class SU acc; ``` --- ## Quickstart ```bash # 1. no install needed — pure Node builtins node examples/demo.cjs # run the full loop with a deterministic built-in world # 2. run a handful of ticks and watch predictions mature + get scored node lib/sentience-loop.cjs --ticks=6 # 3. in your code — bring your own sensors + scorer # const { CognitiveLoop } = require('./lib/sentience-loop.cjs'); # const loop = new CognitiveLoop({ dataDir: './data' }); # loop.addSensor('errors', () => probeErrors()); // () => [{type,severity,detail}] # loop.addScorer('system', (pred) => readGroundTruth(pred)); // -> {actual, correct} # loop.tick(); // perceive→predict→score→surprise→reflect→record ``` > State (predictions, belief-updates, cycle ledger) persists to ./data as append-only JSONL (gitignored, auto-created). Sensors and scorers are the two seams you fill; everything between is provided. The built-in demo ships a deterministic sensor + scorer so the whole loop runs green with zero dependencies and no API key. # Sentience Loop — Architecture

Sentience Loop is a self-monitoring loop built on one idea from predictive processing: a system that models itself should predict, then check. Each tick it PERCEIVES signals from sensors you plug in, PREDICTS a few falsifiable things with a confidence and a test-after horizon, SCORES past predictions that have now come due against what actually happened, treats the wrong ones as SURPRISE (writing a belief-update), REFLECTS on the recent record, and RECORDS the cycle to an append-only ledger. Nothing self-judges: predictions are scored against real observed outcomes, never against the model's own opinion. Bring your own sensors and scorer; a deterministic built-in demo runs the whole loop with zero dependencies and no API key.

## Flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    S["sensors\n(you plug in)"] --> P["PERCEIVE\nsignals"]
    P --> PR["PREDICT\nfalsifiable + confidence"]
    PR --> SC["SCORE\nmatured predictions"]
    SC --> SU["SURPRISE\nconfident miss"]
    SU --> BU[("belief-updates")]
    SU --> RF["REFLECT"]
    RF --> RE["RECORD\ncycle ledger"]
    BU -.-> PR
    SC -.-> RE
    classDef acc fill:#2a3157,stroke:#8B9EF5,color:#fff;
    class PR acc;
    class SC acc;
    class SU acc;
```

## How it fits together

Sentience Loop is a closed predictive-processing loop with two seams you fill — sensors and a scorer — and everything between provided. A `CognitiveLoop` instance persists three append-only JSONL ledgers under ./data (predictions, belief-updates, cycle records). Each tick runs six steps: PERCEIVE — every registered sensor `() => [{type,severity,detail}]` runs; a thrower is caught to ./data/soft-failures.jsonl and skipped. PREDICT — the loop derives a few falsifiable predictions from the signals, each with a confidence and a `test_after` timestamp, deduped by (domain,text) within a 24h window so the same claim isn't relogged every tick. SCORE — predictions whose `test_after` has passed and that were never scored are graded: a scorer you register per domain reads ground truth and returns {actual, correct}; the loop appends an `end` record (scored at most once, keyed on the original timestamp). SURPRISE — every prediction that was confident (>=0.7) and wrong writes a belief-update naming the prior to recalibrate. REFLECT — surfaces the recent contradiction count. RECORD — appends a cycle summary (signal/prediction/scored/surprise counts + duration). `loop.tick()` runs one cycle; the CLI adds --ticks=N and --data. Fail-open throughout: a broken sensor or scorer degrades to a logged soft-failure rather than crashing the loop.

## Extending it

Every capability is a self-contained module. To add your own, follow the contract the existing
modules use and wire it into the entry point. Keep it portable — config via `.env`, no hardcoded
paths, no personal accounts.

## Design principles

1. **Predict, then check.** A claim with a confidence and a test-after time is a measurement; the same claim without them is just a sentence. This loop only deals in the first kind.
2. **Never self-judge.** Predictions are scored against real observed outcomes through a scorer you supply — never against the model's own opinion of itself.
3. **Surprise is the signal.** A confident prediction that missed is worth more than a hundred that hit; each one writes a belief-update and sharpens the next.
4. **Fail-open + auditable.** A broken sensor or scorer is logged and skipped, never fatal; every tick appends an honest cycle record you can read back.

what it does

A loop that grades itself.

01 / PERCEIVE

Sensors you plug in

A sensor is just `() => [{ type, severity, detail }]`. Register as many as you like — a log reader, a metrics probe, a queue-depth check. The loop runs them each tick, collects the signals, and hands a thrower's failure to the soft-failure log instead of letting it crash the cycle. The loop owns the cadence; you own what counts as a signal.

02 / PREDICT + SCORE

Falsifiable, then graded

From the signals the loop emits a few predictions — each with a confidence and a `test_after` time — and dedupes them so the same claim isn't logged every tick. When a prediction's horizon passes, a scorer you supply reads the real outcome and marks it correct or not. Predictions are graded against observed ground truth, never against the model's own judgment.

03 / SURPRISE + RECORD

Wrong is the signal

A prediction that was confident and missed is a surprise — the loop writes a belief-update naming the prior that needs recalibration, so the next prediction is sharper. Every tick appends an honest cycle record (signals, predictions made, scored, surprises, duration) to a ledger you can audit. Reflection surfaces the recent contradiction count. Nothing is hidden; nothing self-congratulates.

# 2. run a handful of ticks and watch predictions mature + get scored
